thesis: Visa is a wide-moat, unlevered network with ROIC at a 2-year high, flat margins and a strong uptrend, a good business that is working, bought on trend strength rather than a discount.
reason: The scorecard reaches 4 on quality, balance sheet, moat and trend strength, not on value: every multiple is above its 5y range, so the bear case's de-rating and interchange-regulation risks are real. Conviction 4 gives the standard core size, volatility-scaled by Python; no cap is breached, so nothing is replaced.

triggers.text: TTM ROIC falls below 45%, giving up most of the rise from 40.1% (FY2022) to 56.4% and signalling network pricing erosion.
TTM FCF margin falls below 42%, extending the slide from 53.9% a year earlier to 48.1% and showing the cash gap is structural.
TTM operating margin falls below 62%, under the flat five-year band around 66.3%-67.2%, showing client incentives or regulation compressing network economics.
A final US rule or court decision materially lowers the Reg II debit interchange cap, or the Credit Card Competition Act is enacted.
